saints.name: Sts. Cornelius and Cyprian
saints.title: Pope and Bishop, Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A pope who died in exile and the bishop of Carthage who defended him, joined in one memorial as martyrs and friends…
biography: Cornelius was elected Pope in 251, in a time torn by the question of how to receive back those who had lapsed under persecution. Against the rigorists he upheld the Church's power to reconcile penitents, and was supported by St. Cyprian, bishop of Carthage. Banished by the emperor, Cornelius died in exile in 253 and was honoured as a martyr.

Cyprian, a converted rhetorician and one of the great pastoral writers of the early Church, guided Carthage through persecution and plague and defended the unity of the Church. He was beheaded outside Carthage in 258. The two friends, united in life and doctrine, are named together in the Roman canon.
saints.knownFor: Upholding the Church's mercy to the lapsed and their witness of blood.
